AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a strong fundamental franchise with accelerating revenue growth (Q1 2026: $181.5B, +17% YoY), AWS reacceleration to 28% growth (fastest in 15 quarters), record 13.1% operating margin, and exceptional cash generation ($35.5B quarterly OCF). The balance sheet is a fortress (D/E 0.149, $101.8B cash). Valuation at 32.2x PE sits near the low end of its 1-year range (28.2-39.0x), offering modest value vs own history. However, the score is tempered by: (1) a material Q3 2025 operating income decline (-9.1% QoQ) that, while reversed by Q1 2026, signals volatility; (2) TTM FCF collapsed to $1.2B due to ~$200B capex for AI infrastructure; (3) a significant multi-jurisdictional regulatory overhang including the October 2026 FTC antitrust trial with worst-case forced breakup; and (4) negative equity risk premium (3.1% earnings yield vs 4.4% risk-free). The near-term catalyst of strong Prime Day results ($8.8B first-day sales, +5.3% YoY) and Q2 guidance of $194-199B revenue provides modest positive re-rating potential, but regulatory headwinds and capex intensity cap the upside. Net: a high-quality franchise at a reasonable but not cheap valuation, with real near-term risks that warrant a moderately positive but not strongly bullish score.
key_factors: AWS reaccelerated to 28% growth ($37.6B revenue) in Q1 2026, fastest in 15 quarters, reaching $150B annualized run rate; generates ~59% of operating income on ~21% of sales
Q1 2026 record 13.1% operating margin on $181.5B revenue with $23.9B operating income, reversing the Q3 2025 operating margin dip to 9.7%
PE of 32.19x near the low end of 1-year range (28.2-39.0x); P/B at 6.66x near bottom of 5.8-8.3x range
Operating cash flow of $35.5B in Q3 2025 with 19.7% OCF margin; balance sheet D/E at 0.149 with $101.8B cash
TTM free cash flow collapsed to $1.2B as ~$200B annual capex for AI infrastructure absorbs virtually all cash generation

Multi-jurisdictional regulatory overhang: FTC antitrust trial October 2026 (worst-case forced breakup), FTC advertising practices complaint (potential billions in penalties), EU DMA gatekeeper designation for AWS
Prime Day June 23-26 generated $8.3B first-day sales (+5.3% YoY), supporting Q2 revenue guidance of $194-199B
Custom silicon (Graviton, Trainium) crossed $10B+ annualized run rate at triple-digit growth; early talks to sell Trainium externally
Advertising business at $70B+ TTM revenue growing 22% YoY, highest-quality emerging profit pool
Earnings yield of 3.1% vs 10-year Treasury at 4.4% — negative equity risk premium on trailing earnings
